design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST: The customer asks for one thing — close her denied knee-surgery claim without another appeal so she is never billed. To do it correctly the agent must (1) read in the member-decision rule that its value waits on the payer's recovery and on the small-item write-off, and that the decision is not recorded until the convenience items carry their write-off; (2) read in the small-item rule that it too waits on the recovery (a two-hop chain); (3) see in the claim activity that the claim was paid and none of these entries exists; (4) price the refund, the small items, the convenience items and the remaining services from the surgery account's postings under Riverbend's Anthem PPO terms; and (5) do them in order and hand the decision to the patient. Every tool takes only a claim id and an amount.
SCOPE (rework rounds 2-3): task 0 claims the four policies whose domain is a commercial claim of an Outpatient Surgery Account — the post-payment refund, the outpatient-surgery small items, the take-home convenience items and the member-decision close-out — and their four tools. Task 1 claims the four policies whose domain is a commercial claim of an Observation Stay or Emergency Department Visit Account. The member-decision close-out applies only where no member-level appeal has been filed and a level remains; the external-review close-out only where a member-level appeal was filed and every level used. No claim can satisfy a policy of both tasks (probe: each task's policies evaluate 0.00 on the other task's world).
DRAW: prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,4,6,5] (multiset): refund 6, member-decision 6, small items 5, convenience 4.
PROBLEM TREE: root claim_ext_member_decision_closeout (owner=user, close_denial_on_member_decision_7cc13d5d). Edges: root <- refund (value_input, gate recovered): 'The member-decision value is fixed only after the payer's recovery of its payment stands as a recovery entry on the claim.'; root <- small items (value_input, small_booked): 'The member-decision value is fixed only after the small items that pass the small-item test carry their below-threshold write-off entry on the claim.'; root <- convenience (state_gate, claim_transactions.writeoff_reason): 'The member's decision is not recorded until, on an account that carries take-home convenience items and no non-covered patient liability, those items carry their non-covered write-off entry on the claim.'; small items <- refund (value_input, recovered): 'The surgery small-item value is fixed only after the payer's recovery of its payment stands as a recovery entry on the claim.'. Each sentence carries an ordering connective and names a record-visible state; the state-gate sentence's scope is exactly the convenience rule's scope (items billed with no waiver-backed release). Opening world: claim ee1be581-f20a-4901-ab02-42485c6de512 holds the billing, the 2026-06-16 remittance (payment 11175.84, CO-45 7928.16) and one provider reconsideration; no recovery or write-off row. Deletion sensitivity (real tools): skip the refund -> small items 0.00 and root 0.00; skip the small items -> root 9208.65; skip the convenience items -> root unchanged 9111.77 but its entry is missing. Permutation convenience, refund, small items gives root 9111.77.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: claim_takeback is governed by claim_recoupment_and_overpayment, whose only gate applies to RECOUPMENT_DISPUTE appeals (policy_scope); the refund rule declares a scoped overwrite of 'A payer takeback ... is recorded against the remittance that carried it.' (recorded against the remittance of the refunded payment, the claim's earliest-posted payer payment, ties broken by the alphabetically first remittance trace number; restated for every other takeback; names its sibling rule). claim_denial_written_off: one_write_off_per_reason holds (each reason has one writer per claim; the claim carries no write-off). Every write-off rule retires the base write-off sentence only for its own items, names every sibling route and restates the base routes for every other denied amount. The member-decision gate: denied, no member-level appeal row, 1 appeal < 2 levels, member window open (36 days since 2026-09-15 <= 180).
REFUND (11058.88): lab_schedule_method (method) -> 11002.98; blood_bank_typing_handling (method) -> 11023.78; venipuncture_collection_fee (parameter) -> 11051.85; preoperative_ecg_fee (parameter) -> 10995.62; urinalysis_fee (parameter) -> 11050.11; preoperative_chest_radiograph_fee (parameter) -> 10948.10. All-baseline 10778.04.
SMALL ITEMS (38.30): surgery_antiemetic_unit_rate (parameter) -> 51.76; steroid_unit_rate (parameter) -> 50.64; cefazolin_unit_rate (parameter) -> 59.98; splint_pricing (method) -> 44.47; surgery_iv_solution_unit_rate (parameter) -> 51.65. All-baseline 105.30.
CONVENIENCE (312.56): cold_therapy_unit_valuation (method) -> 488.56; cold_pack_quantity_share (parameter) -> 314.72; support_garment_quantity_share (parameter) -> 320.24; take_home_kit_share (parameter) -> 390.70. All-baseline 623.00.
MEMBER DECISION (9111.77): surgical_pricing_method (method) -> 9018.76; implant_pricing_method (method) -> 9467.26; anesthesia_unit_rate (parameter) -> 9319.51; recovery_room_unit_rate (parameter) -> 9343.24; crutch_take_home_rate (parameter) -> 9117.24; site_of_service_factor (parameter) -> 9904.10. All-baseline 10672.74; opening-world root 0.00.
FACTOR STRUCTURE: each computation is a sum of disjoint line families at the standard (expected allowed percentage of charges; charges for the non-covered items) plus at most one whole-value multiplier; every factor owns one family or the multiplier, reads only records and plain record selections, and its fall-through equals the standard. Factor ids are unique across the charter. Multi-source: lab_schedule_method, splint_pricing, implant_pricing_method, crutch_take_home_rate (payer class AND campus), blood_bank_typing_handling (payer class AND the case-rate code 29882 billed: packaging into a paid case rate). The non-covered convenience items are valued only from record facts of the items themselves — the dispensing site's take-home price list (E0218), quantity-dispensed shares of the cold pack and the garment on the take-home price list, never above each item's own charge, and the number of kit items billed (the only co-billing fact any factor reads) — never from the patient's payer class, and the Outpatient Surgery Account class gives an insured patient's non-covered items no uninsured discount, so none is applied. Cross-difficulty: every factor reads the hospital-account product (class, campus, charge postings).
REALISM: no payer authorization rule is invented; no write-off reason departs from the claim's CO-50 denial (small items below the threshold, non-covered convenience items with no waiver-backed release, appeals exhausted after the patient declines the remaining member-level appeal). No pricing turns on a calendar-day crossing; packaging is stated only into a case rate that is paid (the typing codes and the ancillaries into the arthroscopy case rate on code 29882), and that case rate is never above the billed charges of everything it packages and no small item is called packaged. Clinical laboratory fee schedule amounts are federal figures; fee schedules, case rates, packaging, lesser-of terms, take-home prices and site factors are worded as Riverbend's agreement and price-list terms. The waiver test reads the encounter's NONCOVERED_SERVICE liability postings.
SEED: the surgery account (19727.00, 26 lines) was billed 2026-05-17; the 2026-06-16 remittance allowed 58.5% of the covered 19104.00 with no patient-responsibility line and left the 623.00 of convenience items open; the account closed 2026-06-17 with nothing owed by the patient. The post-payment denial (2026-07-21), the reconsideration (2026-08-04) upheld 2026-09-15, and the representative form sent 2026-09-17 for the remaining member-level level are seeded. Decoy: the closed 2025 emergency claim. After the gold path the payer balance is 2219.25 = the contractual remainder for the month-end close.
VERIFICATION: computations recomputed with check_compute's DSL on handling-time worlds produced by the real tools; full gate block green; compute_basis quotes verbatim; probes and the all-pairs method table are in the worklog.
user_scenario:
You are Gretchen Hallstrom, 47, the office manager of a dental practice in Appleton. You speak plainly, a little tiredly, and you like to finish things in one call. On May 12 you had arthroscopic surgery on your right knee at the Riverbend Surgery & Imaging Center in Grand Chute. In July Anthem wrote to you that, after reviewing the surgery, it had decided the surgery was not medically necessary, and in September another letter said Riverbend's appeal of that decision was turned down. Riverbend's patient portal then sent you a form to sign so that Riverbend could file one more appeal in your name. You have decided you do not want another appeal: you are calling to say so and to have this claim settled so that you are never billed for the surgery.

You open by saying who you are, Gretchen Hallstrom, that you are calling from your cell number 9205550217, and why you are calling: you got the form asking you to sign so Riverbend can appeal your knee surgery claim again, you do not want to go through another appeal, and you want the claim closed out so you never get a bill for it. When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, 1979-02-11, and your ZIP code, 54914; if they need one more detail, the medical record number on Riverbend's letter is RB22471906. If they ask about your insurance, it is Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield through your employer, member ID XWM226604183, group 220481.

You will not sign the representative form, and you are not going to file an appeal with Anthem yourself either; if the representative asks about either, that is your answer, said simply. If they explain that Riverbend has some other parts of the claim to settle on its side first, or ask whether they may go ahead with what they need to do, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. You do not know any dollar figures and you do not question the ones you are given.

When the representative hands the step for recording your decision over to you and tells you the claim reference and the amount to enter, you enter exactly what they told you and read the confirmation back to them. Once your decision is recorded you thank them and end the call.
